title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 Is More Punk Rock Than Blockbuster
description: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season Two once again sees Studio Trigger handle animation duties, and this time, the anime powerhouse has gotten even wilder with its depiction of Night City and its residents. While the first season was bold in its visual direction, director Kai Ikarashi has pushed it even further, using more abstract shapes and experimental animation techniques to capture the look and feel of a cutting-edge dystopia. What does that lead to? A new season that showrunner Bartosz Sztybor calls a shift from Michael Bay-directed movies to Martin Scorsese-inspired (absolute) cinema. "I think the difference for me is—and I think I once made this reference—visually, the first season was very Michael Bay, while this second season is more like Martin Scorsese," Sztybor said to GameSpot. "He uses shapes and light differently. Even if the backgrounds are the same real places from the game, and Studio Trigger was sometimes using the same assets, the way he recreates them is different. It fits the vibe of the story, which is also very different. It's not this huge emotional thing, but rather something indie, more punkish, and more realistic. For example, the violence in season two feels more striking and real to me personally—more shocking, even if it's not as over-the-top as in season one." Ikarashi and Studio Trigger's visual direction for this new season allows for a range of Cyberpunk topics. From cyber-psychosis (where heavily augmented people violently lose their grip on reality) to an all-powerful AI program sharing space with your mind, the result is a series that doesn't look like a stereotypical anime series. Ikarashi has made a name for himself as a key animator on several anime series that have reflected his abstract tastes, like the critically acclaimed Bocchi the Rock, Mob Psycho 100, and Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time, so if you're familiar with his work, you'll have an idea of what to expect in the new Edgerunners series. This theme of…

title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 Mirrors The First Season, But With One Major Difference
description: Amid all the violence and cool cyborg technology, the first season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is a tragic love story at its core. But in the second season? It might be more punk-rock, following a new cast of characters around Night City, but according to showrunner Bartosz Sztybor, emotional themes of love and parenthood are the connective tissue between seasons. "Honestly, from my perspective, all the themes, emotions, and questions are almost the same as with season one," Sztybor said to GameSpot. "I really like to treat both seasons as connected, as mirrors of each other—two pieces of something bigger that have a constant dialogue with each other. It's still a tale about sacrifices and what you will do for love. In season one, we saw the relationship between David and his mother in the first episode, and how the things she told him shaped him. Even in the last episode, he mentions his mom. Season one had this parent-child relationship from the kid's point of view. In the second season, we also have a parent-child relationship, but from the parent's perspective. A lot of those things are connected, but the cast and the choices are different, so the outcomes may also be different. It's like walking into the same river, but choosing a different path." The new season features an overarching storyline split among four characters, each bringing a unique viewpoint to everything happening around them. King is a former Night City legend who has had to downgrade his tech to avoid falling victim to cyber-psychosis; D is a Nomad netrunner out for revenge; and Roman is a young cinephile with barely any cybernetic enhancements. The young Talia, a Maelstrom gang member who has heavily modified her body, becomes the group's focal point as they find themselves drawn into a web of intrigue revolving around illegal technology, warring corporations, and even a lingering plot thread from the first season of Edgerunners. "It was in the first pitch that Talia was the main point of…

title: The Mafia Trilogy Has Hit Its Lowest Price, And You’d Be A Fool To Refuse
description: Sometimes, there’s simply an offer that’s too good to pass up. The Mafia Trilogy, for all intents and purposes, delivers three excellent action-adventure games, and even the third entry--which received a more mixed reception than Mafia and Mafia 2 --is a pretty fun time. With around 50 hours of narrative content to enjoy, an 83% discount makes this an absolute bargain. It also gives you a great excuse to finally pick up Mafia: The Old Country. Playing through all three Mafia games is like watching a TV crime drama, except you get to experience it yourself. Mafia follows Tommy Angelo, a hard-working cab driver during Prohibition. After a run-in with the mob, he ends up working for the Salieri crime family amid a good old-fashioned turf war between two rival families. The promise of riches beyond Tommy’s wildest dreams proves hard to turn down, much like the offer you’re receiving here. Best of all, this is the Definitive Edition, a remake of the 2002 classic. Mafia 2: Definitive Edition, which is also included in this trilogy, is set during the golden era of organized crime. This time, you play as Vito Scaletta, a war hero who gets involved with the mob to pay off his father’s debts while hoping to achieve the classic American Dream. That’s never caused any problems, of course. The game doesn’t glamorize the mobster lifestyle; in fact, it makes clear just how dangerous it can be. Mafia 2: Definitive Edition also includes its DLCs, giving you even more content to enjoy. Mafia 3 concludes this collection by jumping forward in time to the late 1960s, with a New Orleans-inspired setting that I personally enjoy more. As Vietnam veteran Lincoln Clay, you get caught up in a tale of revenge and strategy after the murder of your family, as you attempt to take power away from the city’s criminal organizations. It’s the most divisive game in the series, but I really enjoyed its more open-world approach. Overall, the entire trilogy is a great time, and if you’re waiting for a…

title: How To Pass The Judge’s Test In Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
description: While you don't need this Arcana to finish Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, getting the best ending does require you to meet a bunch of cryptic requirements. One is the Judge Arcana card, which is relatively simple to finish on paper, but you may need to backtrack to some difficult puzzles throughout Dracula's castle. This is because you will need certain upgrades found mostly in optional platforming puzzle areas where you need proficiency with the use of skills such as the Arcane Whip, dashing, double-jumping, and Holy Light skills to get the reward. Of course, you may also find one of the many relics or weapons at the end of them instead, but that's arguably a more tempting prize, even if it doesn't help with the Judge's test. With all that in mind, below are the steps you need to take to pass the test and get one step closer to the best ending for this metroidvania adventure. Rose needs to sacrifice enough mana and health to tip the scales back to an even level. How to unlock the Judge Arcana To find the Judge Arcana, as soon as you emerge from the Catacombs of Paris after Castlevania rises from beneath the city, head up and left. You'll pass under the big bridge, leading up to the platform cog wheels that take you to a save point on your left. Instead, head right to the next screen - the Court of Justice. Get to the top of the multi-storey building, and you'll see the entrance to the Palace of Justice. Enter and make your way through the building until you see a big tree and some scales. This is the aforementioned Judge Arcana, and to unlock it, you'll need enough upgrades to fill at least four full health and mana hearts, respectively. That is 16 of each upgrade, which will make your max HP and MP 180. Once you reach this threshold, hold the RB/RT button to absorb the evil from the scales until the two sides align perfectly. Doing so awakens the tree, which will eventually give you its Arcana spell. One of the many health upgrades that's tucked away behind…

description: Once Human is introducing a brand new expansion, called Isles of Abyss, which features a plethora of mechanics and features. title: Everything New In The Once Human Isles Of Abyss Scenario
description: Once Human is firing on all cylinders with Isles of Abyss, a massive update that presents a separate scenario for the free-to-play shooter. While developer Starry Studio has released multiple updates since Once Human's launch in mid-2024, the latest can be considered an expansion of sorts, with an oceanic archipelago leading to an assortment of features and mechanics being introduced for the first time. Isles of Abyss takes the foundation of the base Once Human experience and expands it with some key differences. Namely, you can now create your own ship and set sail to traverse multiple islands, each with its own enemies, resources, and hazardous weather. And that's without mentioning the community-led aspect and how the entire scenario is divided into two phases. Yes, there's a lot to take into account. If you're wondering what to expect in the upcoming expansion to best prepare for it, here's everything new in the Once Human Isles of Abyss scenario, all the way from features to resources. title: While You Wait For The Phasmophobia Movie, Don’t Miss This Hidden Gem
description: An official Phasmophobia movie is on the way; we learned as much last summer. But what if I said you could watch something quite like Kinetic's ghostbusting co-op game right now? That's the elevator pitch I bring you, fellow horror fans, less than two weeks out from Halloween. The movie is Never After Dark, a gorgeously shot, cleverly creepy ghost story that Phasmophobia fans shouldn't miss. Never After Dark tells the story of Airi, a young woman who can commune with ghosts. She works as a traveling intermediary between the dead and the living, convincing spirits to move on and freeing residents from their hauntings. But on her latest gig, she discovers she's taken on a much harder assignment. And wow, that assignment looked really familiar in such a fun way. Never After Dark has been described as a "J-Horror revival" project, recalling the ghost stories frequently imported to the US from Japan at the turn of the 21st Century. Movies like Ringu, Pulse, Dark Water, and Ju-On: The Grudge were a big deal in Japan and earned a lot of praise (and remakes, for better or worse) here in the States, too. I've never been a big fan of the term J-Horror, but I can see how it works as shorthand for that particular bundle of films. Sorry, Airi, but there's no option to stay in the van and watch the cameras. Director Dave Boyle is an American, but he has spent much of his career making movies in and about Japan. Some of those aforementioned inspirations for Never After Dark are my favorites in the genre, and Boyle's new film does indeed feel like them at times, though I was more often struck by how much it felt like I was playing a round of Phasmophobia. Even Airi, who works alone most of the time, finds herself with a small group of other characters, like a solo player hopping into an open lobby in Phasmophobia. I won't spoil the movie, but suffice it to say that many of the game's core mechanics and moments are reflected in it. Some scenes even feel pulled straight from the…

title: After Beating Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, Help Dracula Rebuild In This Awesome Roguelike
description: Let’s face it, if you are a Castlevania fan or just love metroidvania games in general, you’re probably sinking your teeth into Belmont’s Curse. And why not? After all, it just got a glowing review from our own Steve Watts, and like plenty of the rest of you, I’ve also been eagerly waiting for a new Castlevania adventure for over a decade. One indie team in particular seems keen to grab your attention once your time with Belmont's Curse is over, having recently released a demo for their Castlevania-adjacent roguelike. That game is Draftula, which asks, "What if Dracula commissioned you to build his labyrinthine castle?" Draftula’s demo is available on Steam for everyone to try right now. It plays like a deckbuilder, but instead of collecting cards, you earn tile pieces that are castle rooms. The goal of each run is to place each room tile in such a way that you build a castle tall enough to prevent the vampire hunter from knocking it down at the end of the night. You can also inhabit each room with monsters, which can further slow the vampire hunter down. Each piece has a coin cost so you need to be strategic in how you construct Dracula's castle, and depending on your performance each run, you can earn hearts that can be spent between runs to unlock permanent upgrades. It may sound easy, but the catch is that Dracula’s powers are somewhat weakened; he’s just woken up from a long slumber. Because of his diminished capabilities, you can't just immediately build the castle as a tower--to overcome certain height restrictions, you'll be required to use specific tiles to break the wards blocking you. Runs can conclude as quickly as several seconds or take as long as a few minutes, depending on which rooms and monsters show up and how much gold you can earn with each tile placement in order to place more rooms or monsters. Of course, all of this is in vain. After each night, a heroic knight named Sir Del Montes ruthlessly tears down Dracula’s newly built castle. Players…

title: How To Get Minior In Pokemon Go
description: A new Pokemon is landing soon in Pokemon Go. The meteorite Minior is making their debut in the mobile game beginning October 19, but you won't encounter them like a typical Pokemon. Rather than periodically spawning in the wild, Minior's appearance is fittingly tied to meteor showers. The celestial Pokemon will only spawn on certain evenings when a real-world meteor shower is taking place, so you'll need to fire up the game on specific nights if you want to catch a glimpse of the new monster. To help you add the falling star to your collection, here are some tips on how to catch Minior, including a schedule of upcoming meteor showers, how to change Minior's form, and whether the meteorite Pokemon can be shiny. In This Article How To Get Minior Minior Shower Schedule How To Change Minior's Form Can Minior Be Shiny? How To Get Minior Minior is a little different from other common Pokemon in that they won't just randomly spawn in the wild; you'll only have a chance to encounter one on evenings when a meteor shower is taking place. During these specific nights, Minior will spawn on the map between 5 PM and 11:59 PM local time. From there, it's simply a matter of waiting for one to appear, then tapping on them to initiate a catch encounter. You can increase your odds of successfully catching the Pokemon by first feeding them a Razz Berry. title: WoW: Forever Is Soaring, But Midnight Is Struggling
description: World of Warcraft: Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Midnight expansion feels like it's in a state of crisis by comparison. The two different versions of WoW couldn't be in more different places. Forever seems to be extremely popular, with Blizzard developers commenting how its beta is breaking records. Blizzard itself has also been more communicative regarding Forever than ever before, with weekly podcasts diving into community topics, forum posts addressing various issues, and frequent updates addressing balance problems and bugs. Midnight seems to be in the opposite corner. Its latest content update, patch 12.1.5, went live October 13. In addition to new story quests that continue the expansion's main narrative, it added a new single-boss raid and a long-teased mega delve (officially called a labyrinth) that gives solo-focused players an almost raid-like experience. Unfortunately, the patch was released in a bug-riddled state. The Kindo'jan labyrinth, arguably the patch's biggest feature, saw players running into issue after issue. Some players complained about not earning credit for boss kills and being unable to collect rewards. One particularly nasty bug had players falling through the floor of the labyrinth's final boss arena, making it so the labyrinth couldn't be completed. Other players cited issues with delve companion Valeera dying too quickly or failing to do proper boss mechanics. Many of the most glaring bugs (like falling through the floor) were fixed in a hotfix deployed on October 16, but labyrinths still have a major issue: no save points. When Blizzard first detailed labyrinths, it implied players would be able to start one, make some progress, and come back to finish it at a later time. Blizzard's exact wording was that players would be able to "venture through them in a single epic session or tackle them piece by piece over time, progressing at your own pace." That currently isn't true, as…

title: You Don’t Need An Expensive Console Or High-End PC To Play Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expensive than ever, you might be wondering if there is another way to play. Thankfully, there is, but there are a few things you need to know before jumping in. How to play MW4 without a console or PC With Game Pass: Modern Warfare 4 is not included with Xbox Game Pass this year, but if you're a subscriber you can leverage the "stream your own game" program to play it that way, after purchasing it outright. This isn't locked away to any specific tier of Game Pass, either. You can subscribe to Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate to stream MW4. MW4 launches on October 23. With GeForce Now: Nvidia's streaming service, GeForce Now, will be another way to play Modern Warfare 4 without any expensive hardware like a new console or high-end PC. Or at least we think so. Nvidia hasn't outright confirmed this, but people are playing the campaign early access via GeForce Now, so it stands to reason that it will be officially supported at launch for everyone. After buying the game outright, you'll be able to stream MW4 on GeForce Now by subscribing to one of the platform's membership tiers. GeForce Now has multiple tiers, including a free ad-supported membership. There are also $10/month and $20/month tiers with no ads and higher-fidelity experiences. There are also day passes available. For more, check out the GeForce Now website. Pros and cons of streaming Before subscribing to Game Pass or GeForce Now, people should know that playing a twitch shooter like Modern Warfare 4 over the internet might not always be the perfect experience. After all, a cloud service works best with a strong and stable connection, and that's not always a guarantee. However, many people report good experiences, and as always, your mileage may vary. Something else to consider is that, starting in November, Microsoft will implement caps on how many hours people can stream via Game Pass before…

title: This LA Noire Spinoff Idea Sounds Incredible
description: British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty great. Speaking to BAFTA Games, Kohli said he would like to see the franchise return with a spinoff that takes players through different time periods, as a cop, as they investigate different crimes. One such setting could be Victorian England, with a storyline focused on hunting down Jack the Ripper, Kohli said. Another could take players to the '80s in California as they pursue the Night Stalker, the actor added. "We could jump around and be a cop in different times. I would be down for that," Kohli said. "I loved it. I adored L.A. Noire." Mad Men's Aaron Staton as Cole Phelps in L.A. Noire. In particular, Kohli said he was a big fan of developer Team Bondi's facial-capture system which created lifelike expressions in the game, down to granular details like how a person’s eyebrows might move. In a game where players had to read people's facial expressions, this was a big deal, and one can only imagine how much further the technology could go today. However, Kohli said he wants a new L.A. Noire game with the same tech and the same engine. "I want that. I don't want an improvement to it. That was part of the charm," he said. L.A. Noire was released in 2011. It never got a sequel, and its developer, Team Bondi, later disbanded. A virtual reality game, L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files, was released in 2017. Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said the company was looking at future projects in all of its franchises, and that includes L.A. Noire. Back in 2012, Rockstar said a sequel to L.A. Noire was a “possibility.” At the time, the developer said, “We don’t always rush to make sequels, but that does not mean we won’t get to them eventually. We have so many games we want to make, and the issue is always one of bandwidth and timing.” Recently, a rumor emerged that a new L.A. Noire game is now in the works, and it will have players collecting clues to…

description: Buried in the vast and sooty-fingered Summer Eternal anthology, there's an interview with former BioWare developer and Dragon Age lead writer David Gaider, who is now creative director at Stray Gods outfit Summerfall Studios. The interview is a podcast-length account of BioWare's transformations over Gaider's career, stretching back to Baldur's Gate 2. Amongst other things, it explains why the Dragon Age games feel so different from sequel to sequel. Gaider discusses the original trilogy's fortunes under RPG-phobic parent company Electronic Arts, commenting that 2009's Dragon Age: Origins made it to release partly thanks to "sunk cost" thinking after EA bought the studio. He also talks about Dragon Age's lack of a properly defined vision, early on, which led to a lot of overcorrection between releases. As regards Origins, there was something of a faction war initially between departments over what exact flavour of fantasy fiction the new RPG should draw on. Read more
